reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown hold Matthew's house was a dwelling the family found once Bethlehem's census crowds had moved on from the manger scene.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Raymond Brown's Birth of the Messiah reads Matthew's silence about any journey to Bethlehem as implying Jesus was seemingly born in the very house the magi later visit.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Raymond E. Brown (d. 1998), The Birth of the Messiah (1977), p. 46.

sides.snippet: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
sides.verseText: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

sides.snippet: She brought forth her firstborn son, and she wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
sides.verseText: She brought forth her firstborn son, and she wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.
